frontier.hypothesis: The slot is a REGISTER SPILL home, not a declaration: at some spelling of this body local-alloc or global-alloc fails to seat a pseudo, assigns it a stack slot, and a later pass removes every reference to it - the only mechanism measured anywhere in this project that produces frame bytes with zero sp-relative traffic.
frontier.mechanism: Every probe in the ledger so far tried to ADD an object and then argue about whether it is honest. The untried inverse is to change register pressure until GCC itself puts something on the stack. s2b's b_p4_sel proved the knob exists and is reachable from truthful C: hoisting the D_800A352C + 1 selector out of the loop changes the function from regs 7/0 frame 104... i.e. it moves the allocator, while leaving vars at 56. reload.c/global.c assign spill homes via assign_stack_local, and get_frame_size counts them whether or not the reload survives.
frontier.next_probe: Solver modality, or forensics with dumps. Run `pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_8006DD94` on the score-21 chassis and read .lreg/.greg for which pseudos are seated and how much slack there is; then use tools/ra_solver inverse_compose.py classify to ask directly whether any C-level lever produces an allocation in which one pseudo is spilled while its references are dead. Measure candidates with tmp/grind/func_8006DD94/s2/fp.py, which reads cc1's own vars= line and is far cheaper than the sandbox.

frontier.hypothesis: The only construct measured to close this function is a volatile unwritten local that must sit BETWEEN two declarations rather than first, and the frozen phantom-frame-slot volatile pad family excludes it purely on form (first-decl position), not on mechanism.
frontier.mechanism: The frozen family at .claude/rules/no-new-park-categories.md:422-435 requires a first-decl `volatile u32 pad[N];`, a !FAKE annotation, ledger frame-forensics, and a _SANCTIONED_UNWRITTEN_PADS row (engine/volatile_cheats.py:746). Its two working exemplars (func_80047EE8 / func_80047FBC pre_pad[8]) happen to have LEADING holes. This function's hole is interior because the 0x2C descriptor already sits at the bottom of the vars region, immediately above the 24-byte arg area. The Judge answered this once, on 2026-09-10 05:59, and refused.
frontier.next_probe: Do NOT re-ask without new evidence. If frontier item 1 is spent and comes back dead, the honest disposition is rotation under the >5 floor title, not a second attempt at the pad. If it is re-asked, the ruling-request must lead with the new fact this session produced - that two independent permuter campaigns totalling 56k iterations find the interior pad and nothing else - rather than with a form argument.

frontier.hypothesis: The hole is a family-wide artefact of ONE shared source idiom (it appears at 12, 12, 20, 20 and 36 bytes across five siblings and at 0 bytes in the two that byte-match or use both rect rows), so recovering the idiom from ANY member closes all five at once.
frontier.mechanism: Five functions in one file, all built around the same 0x2C descriptor at sp+0x18 and the same func_8007352C call, all reserving an 8-aligned region above the descriptor that their own code never touches, at five different sizes. A per-function accident would not size itself differently in each function while starting at the same offset in all of them; a shared declaration block whose members are used to different depths would.
frontier.next_probe: Forensics on the two ZERO-hole members instead of the five with holes - the inverse reading nobody has taken. func_8006BB68 is COMPLETED-C on main and func_800720FC uses both rect rows; diff their accepted/target shapes against func_80069F80 (20-byte hole, no rectangle at all) and ask what the 20 bytes could be that the zero-hole members do not declare. func_80069F80 and func_8006A1A0 are the cleanest test cases in the family because they have NO rectangle: their entire residual would be the hole alone.
